issues.description: Method Stock.findStockIngredient: The template repository declares a method findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) in class Stock, while the problem statement UML and the solution repository define/find a single-argument method findStockIngredient(String name). The template's other Stock methods (add(String) and take(String)) call findStockIngredient with one String argument, which will not resolve against the two-parameter signature in the template. This mismatch causes a compilation error and prevents students from using the API as described in the problem statement and shown in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix:
Provide a single-argument signature public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) in the template Stock class to match the UML/problem statement and the solution. Options:
1) Replace the existing two-parameter method with the single-parameter method that performs case-sensitive name matching (as in the solution).
2) Or add an overload public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { return findStockIngredient(name, true); } that delegates to the two-parameter version. Ensure the add(String) and take(String) implementations call (and resolve to) the single-argument findStockIngredient so the template compiles and matches the specified API.

issues.description: The concept is a method to locate a StockIngredient by name. The problem statement (UML) specifies a method Stock.findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient. The solution repository implements public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (single-parameter). The template repository instead provides public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (two-parameter). This mismatch in the method signature (presence of an extra boolean parameter in the template) forces students to reconcile three different signatures for the same conceptual operation and may block them from following the UML or the reference solution and from implementing SealSaloon methods that call findStockIngredient(String).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template signature match the problem statement and solution. Add an overloaded method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) in the template that delegates to the existing findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (e.g., return findStockIngredient(name, true) or choose a sensible case-sensitivity), or change the existing template method to the single-parameter signature used in the UML/solution. This keeps the conceptual API consistent while preserving any case-sensitivity logic.
